- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts show upward trend bias, often peaking too early or too high after recent spikes.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >75), model tends to overshoot and then gradually correct — but correction is too slow or incomplete.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized; model fails to anticipate sharp downward corrections after peaks.
- Forecast horizon (30d) shows persistent lag: true values often dip below forecast mid-to-late period, suggesting model doesn’t adjust for short-term volatility.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — fails to recognize that recent high prices may be unsustainable or temporary.
- When true values show strong downward momentum after a peak, model continues upward trend, missing the turning point.
- Model underreacts to low-price periods — fails to reduce forecast when recent history shows sustained low values.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the last 5–7 days of the 30d window — model overconfident in late period, underestimating volatility.
